dimension_justifications.soundness: The protocol definitions, endpoint hierarchy, and displayed (b-c)/n calculations are internally coherent, and the paper appropriately restricts its estimand. However, every empirical result is explicitly source-reported/cannot-verify, while the item records, stochastic traces, implementations, registrations, and analysis code are absent. Thus the central empirical findings cannot currently be substantiated. This is a demonstrated evidence-availability failure, not a demonstrated falsity of the reported numbers.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The manuscript is exceptionally transparent, well organized, and precise about endpoint roles, contrast directions, confounding, and scope. Tables 1–3 establish a clear hierarchy, and limitations are unusually explicit. The anonymous eight-page PDF is within the nine-page main-text limit, and §6 contains an AI-assistance disclosure. Repetition of the evidence caveat is noticeable but helps prevent overreading.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The included citation material supports a local distinction from iLLaDA: this paper does not invent confidence-guided scoring but instead proposes a paired finite-pool protocol audit with budget and reveal-order analyses. Conceptual novelty is limited to the audit framing and realized-schedule estimand; implementation novelty is absent; empirical novelty consists of one model × one constructed task bed and is unverified. Incomplete closest-work coverage and limited generality make the ICLR-level significance uncertain.

paper_summary: The paper compares five complete multiple-choice scoring protocols for LLaDA-8B-Instruct on constructed GSM8K-MC pools. Its sole primary endpoint is a reported 13.0-point s_conf advantage over mc_uniform at nominal matched-L scoring draws; secondary analyses report a 2L/2L call-count sensitivity, a 128-draw robustness point, one random-order realization, and a fixed-order aggregate whose direction reverses at answer position 0. The paper carefully defines these as finite-pool contrasts conditional on recorded stochastic realizations. Within the included citation lock, iLLaDA owns the confidence-guided scorer; the claimed distinction is the audit design rather than a new algorithm. All measurements and key provenance objects are unavailable for independent verification.
strongest_verified_contribution: The strongest verifiable contribution is the manuscript's precise conceptual decomposition of a scorer into masking, reveal order, ground-truth feedback, estimator, and call-accounting choices, together with a clear finite-pool realized-schedule estimand and endpoint hierarchy. No numerical empirical contribution is independently verified in the snapshot.
strengths: Section 2 explicitly credits iLLaDA for confidence-guided scoring and avoids claiming scorer invention.
Table 1 clearly separates the sole primary endpoint from post-selected, robustness, and secondary analyses.
Equation 1 and §§3–6 consistently distinguish a realized finite-pool contrast from a population or stochastic-policy expectation.
Tables 3 and 5 use explicit contrast directions, and their displayed percentage-point effects are arithmetically consistent with the reported n and b/c counts.
The aggregate fixed-order result and position-0 reversal are presented together, reducing the risk of an overgeneralized headline.
The paper explicitly disclaims component-level causality, actual-cost equivalence, and cross-bed laws.
The PDF is anonymous and within the page limit, §6 discloses author AI assistance, and all listed snapshot-file hashes match MANIFEST.json.
questions: What systematic primary-source search supports the assertion that iLLaDA is the closest work, particularly across masked-LM pseudo-likelihood scoring, diffusion-model evaluation, iterative-unmasking order effects, Monte Carlo mask estimators, and multiple-choice protocol sensitivity?
Can the authors provide an explicit comparison matrix separating conceptual novelty, implementation novelty, and empirical novelty from each nearest prior work?
Why should a conditional observation on one checkpoint and one constructed GSM8K-MC bed be expected to change broader diffusion-language-model evaluation practice?
Can the timestamped registration, complete hypothesis ledger, sampling frames, prompts, choice-construction records, per-item scores, and E10–E14 crosswalk be released anonymously?
How stable are the random-mask and random-order effects across independently generated realizations rather than the single unavailable traces used here?
Which protocol component drives the primary difference when feedback, masking path, reveal order, estimator, and compute are varied independently?
Does the answer-position reversal survive a preregistered tie-robust interaction analysis controlling for construction type?

issues.location: PDF p. 1, Abstract and evidence notation; pp. 2–3, §3 and Table 2; p. 5, §6; pp. 7–8, Appendix D, Tables 9–10.
issues.observed_evidence: The snapshot demonstrably lacks every item-level result object, the pools and construction code, prompts, implementations, stochastic traces, registration, hypothesis ledger, and analysis code. The manuscript labels every measurement SR/CV, and Table 9 marks E10–E14 missing. Consequently, the numerical claims are cannot_verify; this review does not establish that they are false.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's distinct contribution is an empirical audit, so inaccessible audit records remove the evidentiary basis for its principal novelty and prevent checks of pairing, disjointness, stochastic realization, multiplicity, or even exact protocol execution.
issues.required_fix: Provide a complete anonymous experimental bundle containing sampling frames, constructed choices, prompt bytes, model/tokenizer revisions, implementations and configurations, per-item scores and predictions, mask and reveal traces, registrations, analysis code, environment lock, hashes, and an E10–E14 crosswalk.
issues.verification_test: Validate bundle hashes; reconstruct every choice set and pool assignment; confirm pool balance and disjointness; replay every arm from the frozen model inputs; byte-compare stochastic traces; recompute Tables 3–6, confidence intervals, exact tests, and multiplicity adjustments; verify registration timestamps and endpoint roles.
issues.evidence_needed: The anonymous artifacts enumerated in Appendix Table 10 plus resolvable E10–E14 records and an executable frozen reproduction command.

issues.location: PDF p. 2, §2; pp. 5–6, References; p. 8, Appendix E; citation_lock.json.
issues.observed_evidence: The related-work section positions the study mainly against iLLaDA, with only five bibliography entries total. The citation lock covers four adjacent sources and explicitly states that a bibliography-wide audit remains incomplete. It supports a local distinction from iLLaDA but cannot establish that the audit, accounting, budget, or order analyses are globally novel. Whether uncited work anticipates these elements remains cannot_verify under the supplied material.
issues.why_it_matters: A new application of an existing scorer is publishably distinct only if the paper demonstrates that its audit methodology and findings are not already standard or previously reported. The current narrow comparison does not establish that boundary.
issues.required_fix: Expand §2 using a systematic primary-source audit covering multiple-choice scoring for masked models, pseudo-likelihood and Monte Carlo masking estimators, diffusion-LM evaluation, unmasking-order sensitivity, compute-matched evaluation, and answer-position or distractor-construction effects. Compare each claimed contribution axis against its nearest precedent.
issues.verification_test: For every novelty sentence, an independent checker should locate the cited primary source, confirm the quoted methodological overlap and stated difference, and reproduce a comparison matrix covering all contribution axes. A documented venue/arXiv search should reveal no materially closer omitted work.
issues.evidence_needed: Primary-source PDFs or stable identifiers, a search log with inclusion criteria, verified metadata, source-supported novelty sentences, and a closest-work comparison table.

issues.observed_evidence: The manuscript responsibly states that it offers neither a new scorer nor a component-level causal result. Its conceptual novelty is protocol-audit framing, its implementation novelty is nil, and its empirical novelty is a conditional comparison on one LLaDA-8B-Instruct checkpoint and one constructed benchmark family. This narrow scope is demonstrated; transfer beyond the bed is explicitly unmeasured.
issues.why_it_matters: Even if all reported numbers are correct, bed-local non-interchangeability is a limited observation. Without a general principle, reusable method, or cross-bed evidence, its importance for ICLR is unclear.
issues.required_fix: State conceptual, implementation, and empirical novelty in separate explicit terms, then substantiate broader importance through either a formal/general audit methodology with nontrivial consequences or preregistered replications across multiple diffusion checkpoints, tasks, and independently constructed choice pools.
issues.verification_test: Apply the frozen protocol prospectively to multiple model checkpoints and multiple-choice tasks with independently generated pools; report per-bed paired effects and heterogeneity; test whether the key protocol sensitivity and position interaction persist under preregistered analyses.
issues.evidence_needed: Cross-model and cross-task results, independently constructed pools, predeclared hypotheses, heterogeneity analyses, and a clear account of what knowledge remains novel after comparison with prior work.

issues.location: PDF p. 3, §3 and Table 2; pp. 3–4, §4 and Table 3; p. 5, §6; p. 7, Appendix C and Table 7.
issues.observed_evidence: The primary protocol replacement jointly changes ground-truth feedback, masking path, reveal schedule, estimator, and selection-call accounting. The 2L/2L sensitivity matches only the manuscript's invocation count, not actual resource use, and experiment A14-X3 confirms that the factorial ablation was not run. The paper correctly disclaims mechanism attribution, so this is a demonstrated limitation rather than an overclaim.
issues.why_it_matters: The comparison can show only that two complete instruments differ; it does not reveal which design decision causes the difference or offer actionable guidance for constructing a better evaluator. That substantially limits conceptual and practical novelty.
issues.required_fix: Run a controlled common-harness factorial or one-factor-at-a-time study that independently varies feedback, reveal order, masking path, estimator, selection policy, and compute budget while holding all other factors fixed.
issues.verification_test: First reproduce the complete-protocol contrast, then estimate preregistered paired contrasts for every isolated factor across common items and stochastic streams. Confirm that claimed component effects survive multiplicity correction and are not explained by candidate length, ties, position, or construction.
issues.evidence_needed: A shared implementation harness, factorized configurations, per-item score vectors, instrumented call/resource traces, multiple stochastic realizations, and preregistered component-level analyses.

issues.location: PDF pp. 2–3, §3; p. 4, §5.1; p. 6, Appendix A.
issues.observed_evidence: rand_inject uses one unavailable reveal schedule, and each mc_uniform operating point uses one unavailable collection of mask draws. Appendix A further reports that a process-sensitive string hash makes the nominal random-order seed insufficient for replay. The paper therefore estimates only conditional realized-trace contrasts; stochastic-policy expectations and stability are cannot_verify.
issues.why_it_matters: A single stochastic realization may change protocol rankings or effect magnitudes. Without trace recovery and multi-realization evaluation, it is unclear whether the reported audit reveals a protocol property or an idiosyncratic draw.
issues.required_fix: Release the original traces and evaluate independently generated reveal schedules and mask streams under a predeclared seed or precision rule, reporting both within-item and between-realization uncertainty.
issues.verification_test: Replay the original traces exactly, then run at least 20 independent realizations or a preregistered sequential precision design. Report the distribution and confidence interval of each contrast and test whether signs, rankings, and budget conclusions remain stable.
issues.evidence_needed: Persisted original traces, deterministic seed-generation code, per-realization predictions, seed-aware uncertainty analysis, and predeclared stopping or sample-size rules.

ethics_concerns: No direct human-subject, safety, privacy, or deployment ethics concern is apparent. The principal responsible-research concern is evidentiary provenance, addressed in the issues above. The manuscript includes an author AI-assistance disclosure in §6.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control. It operated read-only on the frozen submission snapshot and consulted no internet sources, parent directories, repository history, prior reviews, author notes, revision records, or target scores.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A complete anonymous E10–E14 bundle independently reproduces every table, interval, test, pool property, and protocol trace.
A timestamped registration and complete multiplicity ledger confirm that the matched-L endpoint and analysis family were fixed before outcome inspection.
A systematic primary-source review establishes that the paired finite-pool, call-accounting, budget, and reveal-order audit is genuinely distinct from prior work.
Preregistered cross-model, cross-task, and independently constructed-pool replications show stable, practically important protocol sensitivity.
Factorial ablations identify reproducible component-level causes, and multi-realization analyses show that conclusions are stable across stochastic schedules.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Independent replay changes the reported effects, intervals, or exact-test results materially.
Pool reconstruction reveals overlap, answer leakage, duplicate distractors, position imbalance, or construction artifacts that explain the findings.
The preregistration or hypothesis ledger shows that the stated primary endpoint was selected after inspecting outcomes.
A closer primary source already reports substantially the same audit or conclusions.
Multi-seed or cross-bed evaluation makes the main effects vanish, reverse unpredictably, or depend on a single schedule.
Instrumented traces contradict the stated call ledger or show that tie handling drives protocol rankings.
review_limitations: The review was restricted to the frozen snapshot and could not consult the internet or the cited primary sources; global novelty and citation correctness therefore cannot be independently established.
The included citation lock is an audit summary rather than the underlying primary-source text.
No raw experimental artifacts were available, so empirical values could be checked only for internal arithmetic and consistency with manuscript statements.
The PDF was inspected through its layout-preserving extracted text and metadata; no external manuscript sources or visual assets were consulted.
